title: Actively refactor god files across the authorized Rust project
summary: Audit and refactor pre-existing god files throughout any Rust project under active authorized work, not just newly touched files.
statement: Whenever carrying out authorized work in a Rust project, inspect the architecture of the project as a whole and actively refactor pre-existing god files and mixed-responsibility modules, including files outside the immediate feature being edited. Treat meaningful architecture remediation as ongoing project work rather than an optional future suggestion. Sequence changes safely around project-specific constraints, concurrent work and verification; record and prioritize any genuinely blocked remediation. This obligation applies within the authorized Rust project, not to unrelated repositories.
rationale: Owner-approved, public-safe Rust source organization policy. Governs structural cohesion and active maintenance without any source-length threshold.

conditions: An authorized Rust project is being created, implemented, debugged or maintained, and this rule has been explicitly selected for the consumer.
exceptions: Do not change unrelated repositories, bypass higher-priority project restrictions, or treat publication of this rule as automatic activation.
Preserve correctness and established interfaces; sequence risky or conflicting refactors safely and report any block without declaring the debt resolved.

bounds.window: each applicable authorized Rust development or assessment activity

exclusions: Do not change unrelated repositories, bypass higher-priority project restrictions, or treat publication of this rule as automatic activation.

provenance.notes: Public-safe generalized architecture rule; historical unrelated rules and prompt generations are unchanged. The rule is inert until selected.
